title: Throughput guardrail allocator and staged prewarm maintenance scheduler
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Maintenance windows and routine node upgrades currently cause unpredictable transient throughput drops for customers on Dedicated pools. Existing drain logic is FIFO and does not reserve throughput for high-criticality tenants, leading to user-visible latency spikes and brief quota violations during fleet churn. Goal: Implement a two-part system that (1) allocates short-term throughput guardrails per-tenant and per-route during maintenance/upgrade events and (2) schedules node maintenance using staged prewarm lanes that prehydrate KV/LM caches and warm model weights before traffic is shifted.
acceptance_criteria: 1) During simulated maintenance events (up to 20% of hosts), 95th percentile tail latency for high-criticality routes should not regress more than 10% from baseline. 2) Throughput reservations are honored: reserved capacity should be available within 60s of drain start. 3) Staged prewarm lanes demonstrate KV hit-rate improvement of >=30% on drained/offloaded requests. 4) Canaries rolled out to 2 dedicated customers with no customer-reported incidents. 5) Monitoring dashboards surfaced with rollback triggers and cost impact breakdown.
tasks: Design throughput guardrail allocator algorithm and reservation tokens
Implement admission controller changes to honor reservations during drain windows
Add prewarm lane orchestration to maintenance scheduler (KV warm, model disk prefetch)
Integrate with autoscaler to express soft-hedges for burst capacity
Create dashboards: reservation usage, prewarm success rate, tail-latency by route
E2E testing harness for synthetic traffic + chaotic drains
Run staged customer canary and collect postmortem
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Evaluated two reservation strategies: strict token escrow vs proportional soft-hedge. Chose hybrid: small strict reservation for P0 routes + proportional hedges for P1 routes.
2026-02-20: PR #1342 created for admission-controller hooks (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342). Initial unit tests added for reservation precedence logic.
2026-02-28: Prewarm orchestration POC demonstrated KV pre-hydration script that reduces first-request latency by ~18% in lab. Need to add model weight prefetch on GPU hosts.

2026-03-03: Integration test failed intermittently under synthetic spike due to race between autoscaler launch and reservation consumption. Added backpressure delay to reclaim tokens until nodes are READY.
2026-03-04: Feature flag gated rollout prepared. Scheduling a small canary for two internal teams next week.
comments: Sofia Rivera (PM): Please ensure the cost analysis is surfaced in the console UI so customers can opt into reservation-based SLAs.
Noah Patel (SRE): Need explicit circuit-breaker to avoid cascading token consumption when multiple pools drain concurrently.
Design review (2026-02-18): Approved the UX flow for offering "Maintenance Guardrail" as an opt-in on Dedicated orders. Link to spec in Drive.
rollback_plan: 1) Flip feature flag off to disable guardrail allocations and revert to baseline drain path. 2) If prewarm lanes cause regression, disable prefetching and fall back to cold-drain path. 3) Auto-roll back to previous runtime release using canary rollback playbook. 4) Notify impacted customers via console banner and customer success playbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reservations could lead to sustained overprovisioning and increased cost. Mitigation: reservations are time-limited (default 10m) and monitored; autoscaler soft-hedges will be used before hard reservations for P2/P3 routes. Risk: Prewarming may fail on some models due to memory fragmentation. Mitigation: add a prewarm health probe and mark nodes as not-ready to avoid routing until warmed.
notes: This ticket pairs with a future PM initiative to expose maintenance SLAs to customers and bill for reservation-based SLAs. Keep implementation extensible so policy engine can accept customer-specific contracts.
